detail:
fnn-bpnc-execute (bp-control.lisp:84-104) runs fnn-quantum-bp (O) around fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked and then, inside the same thunk (the cond arm at bp-control.lisp:~104 is lexically in the lambda), fnn-bplc-reconfigure (bp-listener-control.lisp:95) -> fnn-bplc-drive (bp-listener-control.lisp:~36-80): fnn-tcl-listen bind, socket-close (line 70, retire), and fnn-out 'BP NODE LISTENING' (line 48), 'runtime line' (line 78); fnn-out -> fnn-emit (io.lisp:998-999) = write-sequence then finish-output on *fnn-stdout* (a blocking fd-stream, :buffering :full, io.lisp:~988).
Keys: R2|fnn-emit|O:write-sequence, R2|fnn-emit|O:finish-output (checker counts 13 sites under O; only this one traced; others not enumerated by the checker's output and not individually verified). Same chain also reaches bplc-cut's finish-output/sleep (developer selector FN_BP_LISTENER_TEST_PAUSE_CUT only; test-only pause loop) and socket-close (bp-listener-control.lisp:70), which are baselined/unlisted.
Hazard: a blocked stdout pipe (supervisor not draining) stalls the owner mutex.
fix: Emit the BP NODE lines after the section returns (return the lines as data), and do the listener drive outside the owner section or justify it as a design decision; fnn-out under O is the baseline hazard of every site in the 13.
scenario: BP configuration change through the BP control socket: stdout lines are emitted while O is held; a full stdout pipe blocks the owner.
